what_its_for: This medicine is used to treat opioid use disorder (dependence on opioids such as heroin or prescription pain medicines). It helps reduce cravings and withdrawal symptoms so you can focus on your recovery. Buprenorphine reduces cravings and withdrawal, while naloxone is added to help prevent misuse of the medicine.
how_to_take: Place the film or tablet under your tongue (sublingual) or between your cheek and gum (buccal), depending on your specific product. Let it dissolve completely — do NOT chew it, swallow it, or spit it out. Do not eat or drink anything until it is fully dissolved. Wash your hands before and after handling the medicine. Never share this medicine with anyone else — sharing can cause death in someone who has not been prescribed it.
dosing: Your doctor will start you on a dose that is right for you and may slowly adjust it over time. Most adults take one dose once a day in the morning, but some people may take it twice a day. Always take exactly the dose your doctor prescribed. Do not take more or less without talking to your doctor first. The typical maintenance dose ranges from 4 mg/1 mg to 24 mg/6 mg per day, but your doctor will decide what is best for you.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember on that same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do NOT double up or take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one. If you are unsure what to do, call your doctor or pharmacist.
storage: Store at room temperature between 59°F and 77°F (15°C to 25°C). Keep away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Keep the medicine in a safe and secure place, such as a locked box, away from children and pets. Even a small amount can cause serious harm or death in a child. Do not flush unused medicine down the toilet unless your pharmacist says it is okay — ask your pharmacist about the best way to dispose of leftover medicine.
what_to_avoid: Do NOT drink alcohol while taking this medicine — it can cause serious breathing problems and may be life-threatening. Avoid taking benzodiazepines (such as Xanax, Valium, or Klonopin), sleeping pills, or other medicines that make you drowsy unless your doctor approves, as combining them can cause dangerous breathing problems or death. Avoid driving or operating heavy machinery until you know how this medicine affects you, as it can cause dizziness or drowsiness. Do not use other opioids or street drugs while taking this medicine.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away or go to the emergency room if you or someone nearby experiences: slow, shallow, or stopped breathing; extreme drowsiness or you cannot be woken up; blue or purple lips, fingernails, or skin; confusion, dizziness, or fainting; severe allergic reaction (hives, swelling of face or throat, difficulty breathing); chest pain; signs of liver problems such as yellowing of the skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain. Call your doctor also if you feel your dose is not controlling your cravings or if you are experiencing withdrawal symptoms.
when_it_works: You may start to feel relief from withdrawal symptoms within 30 to 60 minutes after your first dose. Cravings usually begin to decrease within the first few days of treatment. It may take several weeks of regular use before you feel your best. This medicine works best when combined with a full treatment program that includes counseling and support groups. Do not stop taking it suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can bring back withdrawal symptoms.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Tell your doctor right away if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. This medicine can be used during pregnancy under close medical supervision, as untreated opioid use disorder is more dangerous to your baby than the medicine. Babies born to mothers taking this medicine may experience withdrawal symptoms after birth and will need special care. Breastfeeding: Small amounts of this medicine pass into breast milk. Talk to your doctor about the risks and benefits before breastfeeding. Elderly patients (65 and older): Use with extra caution, as older adults may be more sensitive to side effects such as dizziness and confusion. Liver problems: This medicine is processed by the liver. Tell your doctor if you have liver disease, as your dose may need to be adjusted and you will need regular liver tests. Kidney problems: No major dose changes are usually needed, but tell your doctor about any kidney issues.
